scope: Editorial reading journey across all11 current canonical articles

strengths: Specific credited examples establish theatre/radio/literature/film connections without claiming automatic influence.
The overview’s restored-film opening and concluding availability question provide a viable narrative frame.
Companions are substantially self-contained: each names its subject and supplies a concrete film, role or institutional example.
Resident testimony and contrasting criticism in DAMaN preserve needed complexity; attribution and uncertainty should survive tightening.
overall_assessment.main_problem: Accumulated correctness explanations and similar abstract conclusions make different essays sound alike. The overview has a coherent potential story but its late sections increasingly behave like appended topic modules.
overall_assessment.overview_recommendation: Use making/representation/access as an explicit sequence beneath the existing Bologna frame; move transient showtimes out of the durable reading; reduce duplicated festival exposition and align onward links with the ending.
overall_assessment.companion_recommendation: Give each companion a distinct centre and ending: Bhukha livelihood/distribution; Maya survival/reception; Parbati adaptation/credits; Sadhu acting/directing; Manmohan household/property; Nandita family/acting/directing; DAMaN whose account of care; AIR adaptation/listening; TV production labour; OTT commissioning/availability.
retain_boundaries: Do not delete material uncertainty about revenue, announced releases, clinical causation, premiere dates, or image identity.
Do not add scenes, aesthetic judgements or viewing instructions that imply a film has been watched.
Do not expand source-derived passages without rechecking shared source budgets.
Proposed ordering reflects editorial judgement, not new historical chronology.
overview_proposed_order: Radio and literary adaptation through named contributors
Production infrastructure alongside Parbati and actual crews
Selected filmmakers, languages and cross-language artists
Contemporary films, theatres and audiences with concise revenue limits
TV and OTT as brief companion bridges
Preservation and the return to the opening question
overall_assessment.no_uniform_template: Do not force the11essays into identical headings, lengths, opening devices or endings. The distinct subject centres above are alternatives, not a mandatory structure. Maya’s restoration frame and AIR’s listen/read invitation already work; preserve these differences.

articles_read.read_scope: Current narrative, captions, headings, endings and Further reading read directly and sequentially; no prior PASS substituted for reading. Notes used as boundaries, not independently fact-checked.

findings.quotation: This is a journey through several turning points
findings.reader_effect: The introduction promises turning points, but the later combination of awards, commercial reporting, listings, platforms and infrastructure produces several competing organising principles. The Bologna opening/return is a useful spine that can carry the material more clearly.
findings.suggested_action: Keep the Bologna frame. Organise the middle around three questions: how films became possible; whose lives/languages they brought forward; how audiences can encounter and preserve them. Move the existing OFDC and Kalinga/Cinexstasy material beside production or exhibition, rather than introducing a separate institutional roll-call immediately before the ending. This is a proposed order, not a new historical claim.

findings.quotation: A film’s place in this history is different from its availability tonight.
findings.reader_effect: The precise25October2026 showtimes are already a past snapshot on26October. Even with the explicit date, “tonight” and “before travelling” switch a durable history into a booking guide and can suggest immediate usefulness it no longer has.
findings.suggested_action: Move the dated evidence to the research record or a clearly historical availability sidebar; keep one enduring sentence in the narrative: “A film’s reputation and its availability are different questions.” Link to the booking source as a place to check current listings, without preserving old times as travel advice.

findings.quotation: These precise distinctions make the achievement easier to appreciate.
findings.reader_effect: Three consecutive award paragraphs plus their summary pause the household/story thread; the Maya companion repeats the same distinctions in full.
findings.suggested_action: Retain the exact national award and Cannes/Mannheim categories, but combine the overview treatment into one paragraph and link directly to the Maya companion. Cut the quoted summary sentence; return immediately to what these filmmakers were observing. Keep award-year caveats where needed, not generic praise of accuracy.

findings.quotation: - [Odia television and the stories that came home]
findings.reader_effect: The fourteen-link list begins with TV/OTT although the ending explicitly invites Maya then Bhukha. Readers receive a different route from the one the narrative just proposed.
findings.suggested_action: Order Further reading to match the ending: Maya, Bhukha, then two or three explicitly described choices for makers, contemporary cinema and broadcasting. Keep the rest as additional reference links. Distinguish full companion essays from brief person/work records.

findings.quotation: A recent scholarly study by Amrit Amlan Pattanaik approaches Mohapatra’s Sambalpuri cinema
findings.reader_effect: This one-sentence paragraph names a study without giving a distinct insight beyond the preceding Sambalpuri-identity paragraph. It reads as a bibliography entry in the narrative.
findings.suggested_action: Move the study to its note/Further reading unless a precise, already verified argument can be stated. Keep the director’s distribution recollection as the concrete counterweight to international recognition; do not invent scenes to lengthen the essay.

findings.quotation: - [Odia cinema: the world in our own voice]
findings.reader_effect: This is the only film companion that sends readers solely back to the overview. Its livelihood question already connects naturally with other complete essays.
findings.suggested_action: Add one reasoned onward link: Manmohan for another household under economic pressure, or DAMaN for a different account of work and public responsibility. Say what the reader will gain rather than supply a bare list.

findings.quotation: not a claim that it won the Palme d’Or
findings.reader_effect: The reader has not been told of a Palme d’Or claim; denying it inserts an imagined misconception into an otherwise assured account. Precise naming already prevents the mistake.
findings.suggested_action: Suggested wording: “The film was selected for Cannes Critics’ Week in1984. Mannheim’s archive records its shared Grand Prize of the Third World competition, a category distinct from the overall Grand Prize.” Retain citations and the real distinction; omit the unrelated award denial.

findings.quotation: The lesson is practical as well as moving.
findings.reader_effect: The Alanen paragraph is the rare point where a particular response to the film appears. Two generic concluding paragraphs then move away from that experience, repeating the two-journeys opening.
findings.suggested_action: End closer to the restored film: condense the final two paragraphs into “The restoration makes both encounters possible again: with the family Mohapatra filmed, and with the work of the people who kept that film available.” Keep Alanen’s mixed response and attribution; do not turn it into audience consensus.

findings.quotation: A producer’s name, a shared directing credit and a screenplay credit offer different kinds of evidence.
findings.reader_effect: The opening, collaboration section and conclusion all explain why credits matter. The reader understands the premise before the novel/cast example arrives.
findings.suggested_action: Cut this generic recap and one of the adjacent collaboration explanations. Move straight from the named collaborative credits to the novel’s property conflict, then its named cast and crew. Keep colleagues visible through their actual credits rather than repeated statements that collaboration matters.

findings.quotation: Parbati’s achievement needs no inflated award label.
findings.reader_effect: The ending addresses a hypothetical inflation of awards rather than the work the essay has just revealed. The factual film-honour qualification is sufficient.
findings.suggested_action: Retain the exact film-honour sentence, then end on her combined producer/director/performer responsibilities. Suggested closing: “The credits of Chha Mana Atha Guntha return us to the work behind the familiar face: producing a film, shaping its interpretation and playing Saria.”

findings.quotation: ## A career on both sides of the camera
findings.reader_effect: The heading restates “The actor was also a director”; the short essay closes twice, with generic remarks about crossing languages and understanding production.
findings.suggested_action: Merge the final two sections. Keep Abhiman and the later jury role as two concrete developments, then end on Ankur/Abhiman as acting/directing entrances. Remove “The roles belong together” reasoning that generalises what every performer-director understands.

findings.quotation: ## Read the collaborators, too
findings.reader_effect: Readers meet Klanta Aparanha’s technical credits before being told its situation. They have little reason yet to attach significance to those names; the opening’s promise of quiet lives remains abstract.
findings.suggested_action: Move “A household under pressure” before the collaborator list. Introduce Klanta Aparanha through Adikanda/Niru and the dowry mortgage, then show the people who made that story. This gives the short companion a film-centred centre without requiring new research.

findings.quotation: The recognition invites a return to the films themselves
findings.reader_effect: The one-sentence ending could close almost any article in the series. It does not return to the particular household just introduced or explain what to follow next.
findings.suggested_action: End on the existing dowry/property conflict, then link Maya Miriga with a precise invitation to compare two family pressures. Do not imply close-viewing knowledge beyond the catalogue synopsis.

findings.quotation: Das’s own account gives Baripada an emotional place in her life.
findings.reader_effect: The first two sections revisit the same childhood testimony three times, including warnings against an incorrect birthplace claim. The direct Odia acting credit arrives later than necessary.
findings.suggested_action: After the opening, move directly to “Acting in Odia: Biswaprakash”. Cut the second Baripada recap and compress the regional-belonging caveat to one sentence. Her actual acting work makes the connection concrete; readers need not be instructed repeatedly how to claim it.

findings.quotation: The connections are specific: family memory, creative choices, a city on screen
findings.reader_effect: The final summary omits Biswaprakash even though the new acting section importantly changes the article from family connection alone to participation in Odia filmmaking.
findings.suggested_action: Suggested ending: “Baripada belongs to her family memory; Biswaprakash to her acting work in Odia; Zwigato to her return to Odisha as a director. These connections do not confine the rest of her career.” Trim the preceding recap so there is only one ending.

findings.quotation: A separate evaluation followed malaria camps in 15 villages
findings.reader_effect: The indispensable distinction between a fictional doctor and collective care expands into study design and numbers, temporarily turning a film essay into a programme evaluation. This makes the resident’s concrete access account harder to reach.
findings.suggested_action: Keep the2015fiction/2017programme chronology and the fact that programme research does not measure film effects in the main text. Move detailed village counts/comparison design to the existing source note, then bring the health-worker and resident accounts immediately after the critique. Preserve the non-causation caveat wherever the findings remain.

findings.quotation: Sometimes the road outward begins with paying closer attention to home.
findings.reader_effect: After presenting serious criticism about Adivasi agency, the affirmative outward-journey ending does not return to whose attention and whose voice count. It can feel as though the critique was a detour rather than something that changed the reading.
findings.suggested_action: End by holding both gains and questions: “DAMaN brought a story of care in Malkangiri to wider attention. Its reception also asks who gets to tell that story, and how much room it leaves for the people already doing the work.” Retain the distinction that the resident testimony is not film reception.

findings.quotation: It is also a reminder to distinguish Devdas from Gopal Chhotray.
findings.reader_effect: Names are already identified correctly; telling the reader they are not interchangeable sounds like an internal fact-check. Similar caveats recur after stage/radio links and first-broadcast dates.
findings.suggested_action: Keep the correct full names and factual boundaries. Delete this generic reminder; retain the specific lyricist/composer/programme example. Keep the1974edition versus broadcast distinction in the note unless a first-broadcast claim is made in the body.

findings.quotation: There are several ways to explore the older work.
findings.reader_effect: The strongest practical invitation identifies texts and literary readings, but their direct links sit only in sources/Further reading. Readers must leave the paragraph to find the resources.
findings.suggested_action: Link “Odia Bibhaba” and “Chhotray’s readings” directly here and keep the sentence distinguishing author readings from AIR productions. Shorten the last paragraph’s three research questions to one concrete next step: choose a text and compare it with an available author reading, without promising a matching original broadcast.

findings.quotation: A television serial asks them to return to a story.
findings.reader_effect: The appealing serial-focused opening is followed by several chronology/channel-ownership sections before a specific serial appears. The early promise is delayed.
findings.suggested_action: Move the existing Kemiti Kahibi Kaha example just after the introduction as a short anchor, then proceed to the public/private histories and labour accounts. Alternatively change the opening to promise the institution-and-work history actually delivered; avoid inventing a viewer scene.

findings.quotation: ## The people keeping the pictures on air
findings.reader_effect: The2002live-news team is valuable but interrupts the transition from channel development to serial labour without a sentence connecting the different types of television work.
findings.suggested_action: Add a bridge using existing evidence: “The expanding schedules depended on different kinds of teamwork, from a live festival broadcast to a serial delivered on time.” Then keep the named live crew and episode-production accounts as two examples, not interchangeable production models.

findings.quotation: A streamed television episode and an original web series may appear beside one another in an app
findings.reader_effect: The opening, catalogue section, Tarang section and preceding TV article explain the same original/acquired/catch-up distinction. The Chumbak example must compete with repeated instruction.
findings.suggested_action: Define the distinction once in “What enters the catalogue”, then remove the opening duplicate and Tarang’s generic two-activities recap. Bring Chumbak forward as the first test of what a new commissioning space can offer. Preserve the original/exclusive distinction in the definition.

findings.quotation: The next chapter is therefore open.
findings.reader_effect: The final paragraph repeats the series-wide promise of new voices/older works without returning to the creator budgets or availability problems that make this essay distinct.
findings.suggested_action: End on the existing practical criterion: “For viewers, the question is whether a film remains findable and accessible. For makers, it is whether the payment and rights arrangements help finance the next one.” Link the audience-access section back to the overview’s cinema-hall question rather than repeat a broad future promise.

suggested_revision_order: Nandita repeated introduction and ending update
Each remaining companion: remove one repeated methodological recap and give one distinct ending
Align Further reading with the promised route; preserve reference records separately
limits: Suggestions only; no factual re-research or publication decision.
No browser layout judgement; this is a text/read-path audit.
Line numbers and hashes identify the audited snapshot; later edits may move them.
